scope: Proposition 4.2 (Perturbations enforcing GG) of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use (4.1), and fix the finite cascade partition and a compact range of the other parameters. The following two procedures give limiting arrays with deterministic diagonals and joint Ghirlanda–Guerra identities for (A1, . . . , Am, T). 1. Choose a deterministic minimum of −EPenr N (t, h, u, v) + JN (t, h) + ΠN (u, v), ΠN = ∑︂ j≤N 2−j (uj − 3/2)2 + ∑︂ a (va − 3/2)2 , over any compact set of the other parameters and (u, v) ∈ [1, 2]N+m; here JN is independent of u, v. Every subsequential overlap limit at these minima, after a further subsequence for the diagonal means, has the stated properties. 2. Fix any deterministic sequence of the other parameters and integrate over product uniform probability η on Θ = [1, 2]N × [1, 2]m, ignoring uj for j > N. There are measurable sets GN ⊂ Θ with η(GN ) → 1 such that every sequence θN ∈ GN has the same properties at each subsequential overlap limit, after selecting convergent diagonal means. These assertions hold for every deterministic prior described above. They remain valid when t = tN and the bounded enrichment parameters vary with N.
